requirement: R2 — MOTIF / CLUSTER VIEW. Given a motif (arrived at either as a specific instance from the R1 transcript view, or as a cluster id from browse/network/search), show: (a) which cluster it belongs to and what that cluster looks like as a sequence object (logo/consensus, positional distribution, size, composition); (b) how that cluster associates with protein features on the other modality — the ranked partner clusters, their NPMI/APC statistics, their enriched protein features, and whether each association survived or failed the four-condition phylogenetic-independence gate; (c) every annotation attached to the motif and to its cluster, with source, denominator, effect size and FDR. The view must remain informative — never blank, never misleading — across the large coverage gaps measured in this dataset: 434 of 900 clusters have no PWM, 437 have no term at FDR<0.05 (499 under the authors' own mandated triple gate), 387 have no module, and 282 of 600 UTR clusters have zero partners passing the phylo filter.

units.name: Cluster identity header with three-tier name
units.what_it_shows: The cluster's id, region, module, size, and a human-readable name that is never a bare id — plus an explicit badge naming which of three naming tiers produced it.
units.encoding: Title line (name in serif, id in mono); tier badge with three distinct fills: 'curated' (37 clusters), 'top enriched term' (426 more), 'derived descriptor' (437). Region and module chips in the published palette.
units.data_source: Tier 1: .../figure3_4/motif_pair_network/intermediate/cluster_term_labels.csv (65 rows, 37 distinct clusters — I verified; cols cluster, display, source, fold, rank). Tier 2: intermediate/cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz top row by fdr_cluster after dedup. Tier 3: intermediate/consensus_meta.csv consensus + base composition from motif_full_annotations.parquet.motifs + n_instances.
interactions: hover tier badge -> how this name was derived, with the tier's cluster count
click id -> copy
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 463 of 900 clusters have a significant term to name them and 437 do not. Without a three-tier rule, roughly half of all R2 pages open with 'utr3_0342' as their title, which makes the view unusable for browsing. The tier badge is what keeps a synthesised descriptor from being mistaken for a finding.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — resolve all 900 names at build time into clusters.json; tier 3 requires computing base/residue composition per cluster from the motifs column.
units.prior_art: Pfam/InterPro entry pages, which always carry a short name plus a curation-status badge.

units.name: Arrival-context banner (the instance you clicked)
units.what_it_shows: When R2 is reached from a motif span in R1, the specific instance that brought the reader here: gene, transcript, coordinates, its own sequence, and how it sits inside the cluster's distributions.
units.encoding: Slim banner above the header: mono sequence, gene/transcript chip, and three inline percentile ticks (this instance's motif_score, motif_entropy, and length against the cluster's own distribution).
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet row at raw_motif_index (gene_symbol, sequence_id, motif_start, motif_end, motifs, motif_score, motif_entropy, plddt); cluster quantiles precomputed per cluster.
interactions: 'back to ACTB' returns to the exact highlighted span
dismiss to see the generic cluster page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: R2 is defined as 'for a motif', not 'for a cluster'. Every one of the four candidate designs routes /gene -> /cluster and then drops the instance entirely, so the reader loses the thing they clicked. This banner is the only unit that keeps the instance present, and the percentile ticks answer the immediate question 'is my motif typical of this cluster?'
units.precompute_needed: No — instance row is already loaded; cluster quantiles come from the cluster shard.
units.prior_art: gnomAD variant pages, which keep the queried variant pinned while showing gene-level context.

units.name: Hierarchy breadcrumb (instance -> uid -> cluster -> module)
units.what_it_shows: Where the reader is in the four nested motif objects, with the count at each level.
units.encoding: Chip trail: instance (1 of 889,215) / unique_motif_id (1 of 577,186) / cluster (1 of 900) / module (1 of 6, or a grey 'no module').
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet counts; modules.json expanded to a 513-cluster map.
interactions: click a level -> that level's view
hover the uid chip -> the contextual-embedding warning
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 34,110 unique_motif_ids (5.91%) sit in more than one cluster — 'CTGGA' spans 176. Readers will otherwise assume a motif string maps to one cluster. The breadcrumb is where that trap becomes visible without a methods detour.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Per-cluster paralog/ZNF artifact badge
units.what_it_shows: What fraction of this cluster's carrier genes belong to the KRAB-ZNF expansion — a per-cluster artifact risk that exists nowhere in the shipped data.
units.encoding: Small badge on a 0-1 scale with three bands (low <0.05 / elevated 0.05-0.20 / high >0.20), showing the raw fraction and the gene count.
units.data_source: COMPUTED BY ME from motif_full_annotations.parquet: distinct (motif_cluster, gene_symbol), gene_symbol matching ^ZNF|^ZFP|^ZSCAN|^ZKSCAN. Measured: median 0.0129, p99 0.884; 16 clusters >0.20, 14 clusters >0.40. Top: prot_0148 0.973, prot_0228 0.973, prot_0043 0.969, utr3_0176 0.962, utr5_0020 0.935.
interactions: hover -> the ZNF gene list and why paralogy inflates co-occurrence
click -> the methods paralogy section
units.why_it_earns_its_place: All four designs surface frac_co_ZNF per EDGE only, so a reader can open prot_0228 — a cluster that is 97.3% ZNF genes — and see nothing unusual until they click an edge. prot_0228 x utr5_0020 is precisely the #1 raw-NPMI pair the authors annotate as 'ZNF clade artifact'. Both of its endpoint clusters are >93% ZNF, so the risk is a property of the node, and labelling it at the node is more honest and cheaper than waiting for the edge.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — one groupby at build time into clusters.json. A proper version should use the 36 protein classes from the TF-IDF/Louvain families rather than a symbol regex; the regex is a defensible v1 proxy and should be labelled as such.
units.prior_art: gnomAD's flag system, where a locus carries quality warnings independent of any individual query.

units.name: Sequence logo from STREME PWM
units.what_it_shows: The cluster's discovered motif as an information-content logo — the expected centrepiece of any motif-cluster page.
units.encoding: Bits-scaled stacked letters, y-axis in bits (0-2 for RNA over ACGU, 0-log2(20) for protein over the 20 aa). Nucleotides A #009E73 / C #0072B2 / G #E69F00 / U #D55E00; amino acids by the examples_lib.aacol scheme. Width 5-12 (measured min 5, median 5, max 12).
units.data_source: .../intermediate/consensus_repertoire.pkl — per cluster {n_sig, n_found, n_discovery_instances, motifs:[{w, nsites, evalue, pvalue, consensus, coverage, pwm ndarray}]}. Verified: 513 clusters, 451 with n_sig>0, 1,226 motifs total; the 62 with n_sig==0 have an EMPTY motifs list and are all protein.
interactions: hover a column -> the per-position probability vector as a mini bar chart
switch between the cluster's multiple consensus
export SVG and MEME-format PWM
units.library: custom SVG renderer (~120 lines) or logomaker for print export
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the single most expected element of a motif cluster page, and the PWMs already exist. Rendering as SVG rather than a pre-rendered image matters because pre-rendered logos exist for only ~100 of 900 clusters.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — round PWMs to 4 dp and emit as JSON (~0.56 MB for 451 clusters). Note rep[cluster]['motifs'] is empty for n_sig==0, so the loader must handle an empty list, not just a missing key.

units.name: Logo selection rule and quality badge
units.what_it_shows: Which of a cluster's stored motifs is being shown as 'the' logo, and whether that motif is actually trustworthy — its E-value, site count, and coverage.
units.encoding: Badge under the logo reading e.g. 'STREME · E=9.2e-14 · 394 sites · covers 51% of members'. Amber tint when E>0.05, when nsites<20, or when coverage<0.25.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl motif fields evalue, nsites, coverage, pvalue.
interactions: hover -> what each number means
a 'show all N motifs' expander listing every stored motif with its own quality row
units.why_it_earns_its_place: MEASURED TRAP no design caught: 442 of the 1,226 stored STREME motifs have evalue > 0.05 — stored but NOT significant. Naively rendering motifs[0] shows a non-significant motif for 50 of 451 clusters and a thin one (nsites<20) for 24. Selecting best-by-coverage instead improves this to 78 non-significant and 23 thin, so the selection rule must be explicit AND the residual must be badged. nsites goes as low as 3; a three-site logo presented without a badge is a fabrication.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — pick the display motif at build time (recommend: highest coverage among evalue<=0.05; fall back to highest coverage overall with an amber badge) and store the choice so the UI is deterministic.

units.name: Coverage bar with plain-language explainer
units.what_it_shows: What fraction of the cluster's own members the displayed consensus actually matches — the number that stops a logo being read as 'the site in your gene'.
units.encoding: Horizontal 0-1 bar directly beneath the logo, with the percentage in text and a cohort tick at the corpus median (0.534). Bar turns amber below 0.30 and carries an inline caution below 0.25.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv columns coverage, carriers (1,226 rows / 451 clusters). MEASURED best-consensus-per-cluster coverage: median 0.534, p10 0.215, p25 0.377, p75 0.709, p90 0.880, min 0.010.
interactions: hover -> 'coverage = fraction of this cluster's instances matched at >=0.5 bits/position by this consensus'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: MEASURED: 43.9% of the 451 clusters with a consensus have a best coverage below 0.5; 16.6% below 0.3; 9.5% below 0.2. The brief explicitly names this as a place a unit becomes misleading, and the measurement shows it is not an edge case but nearly half the population. Without this bar the logo silently over-claims on ~200 cluster pages.
units.precompute_needed: No — coverage ships in consensus_meta.csv.

units.name: Low-coverage logo demotion state
units.what_it_shows: For clusters whose best consensus covers under ~25% of members, the logo is demoted from headline to evidence: shown smaller, beside the composition fallback rather than above it, with a one-line statement of what it does and does not represent.
units.encoding: Two-up layout: half-size logo on the left, top-k-mer table on the right, joined by a caption 'this consensus describes 18% of the cluster's 640 members'.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv coverage; motif_full_annotations.parquet motifs value_counts for the k-mer side.
interactions: 'promote logo' override for users who want it large anyway
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A coverage badge under a full-size logo is still read as a caption on a headline. 43 of 451 clusters have a best coverage below 0.20 — for those the honest visual hierarchy is different, not just annotated differently. Demotion is the design response to the brief's own warning about 20% coverage.
units.precompute_needed: No — a threshold on an existing field.

units.name: Consensus repertoire table
units.what_it_shows: All of a cluster's discovered consensus (1-10, median 2) with coverage, carrier count and E-value, so a reader sees whether the cluster has one signature or several.
units.encoding: Rows: cid, consensus in mono (RNA alphabet), coverage bar, carriers count, E-value. Selected row drives the logo above.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv (cid, cluster, module, region, consensus, coverage, carriers) joined to consensus_repertoire.pkl for evalue/nsites. Verified rows-per-cluster: {1:120, 2:107, 3:91, 4:75, 5:40, 6:12, 7:4, 9:1, 10:1}. carriers median 232, min 3, max 2,242.
interactions: click a row -> the logo switches
sort by coverage or carriers
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 331 of 451 clusters have more than one consensus. Showing only the top one implies a unimodal cluster that frequently is not one, and hides the sub-motif structure that the consensus-level pair scores later depend on.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Consensus heterogeneity indicator
units.what_it_shows: Whether a cluster's multiple consensus are variations on one theme or genuinely different sequences — i.e. whether the k-means bucket is coherent.
units.encoding: A small similarity chip beside the repertoire table: 'coherent' when the cluster's consensus share a dominant composition, 'heterogeneous' when they do not, with the pairwise consensus similarity shown as a tiny matrix on hover.
units.data_source: consensus_meta.csv consensus strings; similarity computed at build time (simple k-mer cosine or edit distance is sufficient — TOMTOM from the same MEME install would be the rigorous version).
interactions: hover -> the pairwise matrix
link to the length histogram, which is the other heterogeneity signal
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Clusters are k-means buckets over motif embeddings, not curated families. A cluster whose consensus are 'UUUUU' and 'GCCACC' is telling the reader something important about the clustering that no other unit on the page conveys. It is the difference between 'this cluster has a motif' and 'this cluster has motifs'.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — pairwise similarity for the 331 multi-consensus clusters, trivial cost.

units.name: Logo provenance badge
units.what_it_shows: Whether the displayed sequence object is a real STREME fit, a build-time-derived PFM, or absent — so the portal can never silently disagree with the published figures.
units.encoding: Badge: 'STREME v5.5.9' / 'derived from member instances — not a STREME motif' / 'no significant motif found'.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl n_sig, n_found, n_discovery_instances; STREME invocation recorded from motif_pair_network/16_consensus_repertoire.py.
interactions: hover -> the exact STREME command line and background file used
units.why_it_earns_its_place: If the STREME gap-fill is run, ~700 of 900 clusters will have PWMs but only 466 of them will match the matrices behind the published figures. A reader comparing the portal to Fig 3e needs to know which is which, and provenance is the only thing that lets the portal add coverage without contradicting the paper.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Composition fallback: top member k-mers
units.what_it_shows: For the 434 clusters with no PWM at all, the most frequent literal member motif strings with counts — honest, computable today, and explicitly not a consensus.
units.encoding: Ranked mono list with count bars and percent-of-cluster, headed 'most frequent member sequences (not a consensus)'.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet motifs column, value_counts within motif_cluster. Verified 434 clusters have no PWM anywhere (utr3 251, prot 149, utr5 34).
interactions: click a string -> filters the member table to instances carrying it
'search this string corpus-wide'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 48% of cluster pages would otherwise have no sequence object at all. This is the only fallback that needs no new computation and makes no claim the data cannot support.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — top 12 strings per cluster into the cluster shard.

units.name: Member length histogram with modal-fraction callout
units.what_it_shows: How heterogeneous the cluster's member lengths are — and therefore why members cannot simply be stacked into a logo.
units.encoding: Bar histogram over motif_length with the modal length marked and the modal fraction printed as a sentence.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet motif_length grouped by motif_cluster. MEASURED per cluster: distinct lengths median 42 (min 10, max 79); modal fraction median 0.225 (p10 0.142, p90 0.389, max 0.967); only 32 of 900 clusters reach modal fraction >=0.5, 214 reach >=0.3. Median member length 8, max 50.
interactions: click a bar -> filters members to that length
hover -> count and percent
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the visual proof of a methodological constraint that would otherwise be an unsupported assertion. A reader who wonders why the page shows a 5-mer logo for a cluster whose members are 5-50 nt gets the answer here rather than doubting the page.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — a 20-bin histogram plus modal stats per cluster.

units.name: Composition ring (nucleotide / amino-acid)
units.what_it_shows: The base or residue composition of the cluster's members — what makes 'AU-rich' or 'GC-rich' a checkable claim rather than a label.
units.encoding: Donut in NT_COLORS (A #009E73, C #0072B2, G #E69F00, U #D55E00) or amino-acid class colours, with percentages and a GC readout for UTR clusters.
units.data_source: Computed from motif_full_annotations.parquet motifs strings per cluster. Cross-check available for 140 clusters against .../tf_modules/intermediate/utr_composition.csv (fA, fC, fG, fT, GC, ARE_per_knt, polyU_per_knt, Gtract_per_knt, PAS_per_seq).
interactions: hover -> exact fractions
compare toggle against the region cohort mean
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Composition is available for all 900 clusters when a logo is available for only 466, so it is the one sequence-character signal with universal coverage. It also directly substantiates the M1-vs-M2 AU-rich/GC-rich distinction (measured M1 utr3 mean GC 0.344 vs M2 0.497).
units.precompute_needed: Yes — per-cluster composition into clusters.json.

units.name: RNA/DNA alphabet toggle
units.what_it_shows: UTR sequences and motif strings as RNA (U), matching every motif name the manuscript uses, or as the stored DNA alphabet.
units.encoding: Two-state segmented control; RNA is the default. Never applied to protein sequences, where U is selenocysteine.
units.data_source: Storage is DNA-only (verified: utr5 and utr3 motif alphabets are A/C/G/T with zero U). STREME consensus strings in consensus_meta.csv are already RNA (U), so the two layers disagree by default.
interactions: toggle re-renders logo letters, consensus strings, k-mer table and member sequences
search accepts both and normalises to T before matching
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The consensus table ships RNA and the member table ships DNA. On the same page, 'UCUCC' and 'TCTCC' will appear side by side as if they were different motifs unless one convention is imposed. A reader typing the manuscript's UCUCC gets zero hits without normalisation.
units.precompute_needed: No — display-time transliteration.

units.name: Aligned member preview strip
units.what_it_shows: A handful of actual member instances aligned on their best PWM match, so a reader sees what the logo abstracts.
units.encoding: 8-12 mono rows, matched window upper-case and tinted, flanks lower-case grey, all aligned to a fixed column; a bits score per row.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet motifs + the cluster PWM; per-instance best-window score computed with the same coverage() definition (COV_BITS=0.5, uniform background) used in motif_pair_network/16_consensus_repertoire.py so numbers match the published coverage. Schema precedent exists in m4_motif_examples/m4_motif_instances.csv (matched_window, match_start, bits, exact).
interactions: 'show more' pages through members
sort by bits
click a row -> that instance's transcript
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the standard way to show what a motif cluster actually contains, and it is the only unit that lets a reader audit the coverage number rather than trust it. STREME's own sites.tsv cannot be used for this — its seq_ID is an integer index into a score-sorted, 1200-capped discovery FASTA with headers '>0','>1', so it is orphaned from gene identity.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — slide each cluster's display PWM over its members, store (raw_motif_index, offset, bits). This is new computation, but it is the same function the pipeline already runs.

units.name: Logo column probability tooltip
units.what_it_shows: The full letter-probability vector at one logo position.
units.encoding: Mini horizontal bar chart of the 4 or 20 probabilities, sorted descending, inside the tooltip.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl motifs[].pwm rows (verified shape w x 20 protein, w x 4 RNA; rows sum to 1.0000).
interactions: hover a logo column
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Information-content height compresses two things — how peaked the distribution is and which letter wins. A reader judging whether position 3 is 'C or nothing' versus 'C or U' cannot recover that from stack height alone.
units.precompute_needed: No — the PWM is already loaded for the logo.

units.name: No-logo empty state
units.what_it_shows: For clusters with no PWM, an explicit statement of why, with the population count, rather than a missing panel.
units.encoding: Bordered card: 'STREME was not run for this cluster' or 'STREME found no significant motif (E>0.05) among N discovery instances', plus '434 of 900 clusters are in this state' and a pointer to the fallback below.
units.data_source: consensus_repertoire.pkl membership and n_sig; the 513-cluster STREME scope from intermediate/consensus_scope_clusters.csv. Verified: 62 module clusters have n_sig==0 and all 62 are protein; 387 clusters were never run.
interactions: link to methods explaining the 513-cluster scope
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The two reasons for a missing logo are scientifically different — 'not attempted' versus 'attempted and found nothing' — and the second is itself a result about the cluster. Collapsing them into a blank panel discards information and reads as a bug.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Positional histogram along the region
units.what_it_shows: Where along its region this cluster's motifs fall — the evidence behind 'cap-proximal', 'at the start codon', 'mid-protein'.
units.encoding: 20-bin bar chart over relative position 0-1, x-axis labelled 5' and 3' (or N and C), with a median tick and the median value printed.
units.data_source: COMPUTABLE FOR ALL 900 CLUSTERS: relpos = (motif_start+motif_end)/2 / region_length, joining motif_full_annotations.parquet to the deduplicated GRCh37_latest_rna_sequence_pairs_long_transcript.parquet (18,093/18,093 join, 0 out-of-range). Validate against the 142 clusters already in intermediate/streme_pos_cache_all6.pkl (pos_hist, median_pos, n_instances) — I confirmed utr3_0215 pos_hist sums to 566 = n_instances, median_pos 0.4441.
interactions: click a bin -> filters the member table to that positional decile
hover -> count and position range
toggle relative vs absolute nt from the region 5' end
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is one of only three universal signals (with size and composition) available for every cluster, and it carries real scientific content the manuscript relies on. The on-disk cache covers 142 clusters; recomputing all 900 costs ~84 KB and closes the gap entirely.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — 20-bin histogram + median for all 900. Validate the 142 overlapping clusters reproduce the published pos_hist before shipping.

units.name: Positional histogram versus region cohort
units.what_it_shows: Whether this cluster's positional bias is distinctive or just the background shape of motifs in that region.
units.encoding: The cluster's 20-bin histogram drawn over a faint grey silhouette of the pooled distribution for all clusters of the same region, both normalised to density; a one-line KS or median-shift readout.
units.data_source: Same relpos computation, pooled per region. Region means measured: protein 0.497, utr3 0.501, utr5 0.483 — i.e. the background is close to uniform, so departures are meaningful. Per-cluster median relpos ranges 0.004 to 0.997 (p10 0.217, p90 0.673).
interactions: toggle the cohort overlay
hover -> both densities at that bin
units.why_it_earns_its_place: No design included a baseline, and a bare histogram invites over-reading. Because the pooled background is nearly uniform, the overlay is cheap and makes 'cap-proximal' a visible departure rather than an assertion — which is exactly what distinguishes utr5_0079 from an ordinary 5'UTR cluster.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — three pooled region histograms, ~1 KB total.

units.name: Landmark-anchored position track
units.what_it_shows: For UTR clusters, distance from the biologically meaningful landmark rather than from the region edge: nt from the cap for 5'UTR, nt from the stop codon for 3'UTR, nt to the start codon.
units.encoding: A second histogram in absolute nucleotides on a log-ish axis, with the landmark at 0 and a note naming it.
units.data_source: motif_start/motif_end plus region lengths from the GRCh37 sequence parquet; the 5'UTR-to-ATG distance is (utr5_len - motif_end), the 3'UTR-from-stop distance is motif_start.
interactions: switch landmark
brush a distance window -> filters members
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Relative position confounds long and short UTRs. The Kozak claim for utr5_0004 is specifically about proximity to the start codon in nucleotides — a relative-position histogram at median 0.79 understates it, because a 0.79 position in an 84-nt 5'UTR and a 4,705-nt one mean completely different things. This is the unit that makes the M6 story checkable.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — absolute-distance histograms per cluster, two per UTR cluster.

units.name: Cluster size stat block
units.what_it_shows: Instances, distinct genes, distinct transcripts and distinct unique_motif_ids for the cluster.
units.encoding: Four stat rows with the value and a percentile tick against the 900-cluster distribution.
units.data_source: groupby('motif_cluster') on motif_full_annotations.parquet. MEASURED: n_instances mean 988, median 920, min 218 (utr3_0359), max 5,755 (utr3_0188); n_genes mean 597, median 565, min 23 (prot_0092), max 4,532; n_unique_motif_ids median 786.
interactions: hover a stat -> its corpus distribution as a mini histogram with this cluster marked
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Every enrichment fold and every coverage fraction on the page is relative to these denominators. Without them the reader cannot calibrate anything else. The reassuring measured fact is that no cluster is tiny — the minimum is 218 instances — so no page is statistically hollow.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — into clusters.json.

units.name: Sequence redundancy meter
units.what_it_shows: How much of the cluster's apparent size is distinct sequence versus the same string recurring — n_unique_motif_ids / n_instances.
units.encoding: A single 0-1 bar with the corpus median marked, labelled 'distinct sequences per instance'.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet unique_motif_id nunique / size per cluster. MEASURED: median 0.929 — most clusters are dominated by distinct strings, so a low value is genuinely unusual and worth flagging.
interactions: hover -> the count of instances and the count of distinct strings
click -> the k-mer table sorted by recurrence
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A cluster of 900 instances that is really 90 strings repeated ten times is a different object from 900 distinct strings, and no other unit distinguishes them. Because the corpus median is 0.929, this reads as a clean anomaly detector rather than noise.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — one ratio per cluster.

units.name: Gene concentration bar
units.what_it_shows: Whether one gene supplies a disproportionate share of the cluster's instances.
units.encoding: Top-5 genes as horizontal bars showing their share of instances, with the corpus p99 marked as a reference.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet (motif_cluster, gene_symbol) counts. MEASURED top-gene share: median 0.0101, p90 0.0303, p99 0.078, max 0.166; only 6 of 900 clusters have a single gene supplying >10% of instances.
interactions: click a gene -> its transcript view
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the within-cluster analogue of the clade-concentration idea that the phylo filter applies between clusters, and it is reassuring almost everywhere (median 1%), which makes the 6 exceptions worth seeing. Cheap, and it forecloses a reviewer question.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — top-5 gene shares per cluster.

units.name: Score / entropy / pLDDT distributions versus corpus
units.what_it_shows: Where this cluster's members sit on the model's own confidence axes relative to all motifs.
units.encoding: Three horizontal violins (two for UTR clusters), each with the corpus distribution as a faint ghost behind and the cluster median as a tick. motif_score axis MUST be negative-domain (measured corpus min -4.831, median -1.135, max ~0). pLDDT axis MUST be 0-1, not 0-100 (measured min 0.1, median 0.8, max 1.0).
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet motif_score, motif_entropy, plddt grouped by motif_cluster. MEASURED per-cluster medians: motif_score -2.900 to -0.009; motif_entropy 0.044 to 2.847; plddt (300 protein clusters) 0.215 to 0.972, median 0.801.
interactions: brush a score range -> filters the member table
hover -> quartiles and percentile within the corpus
units.why_it_earns_its_place: pLDDT cluster medians spanning 0.215-0.972 is a genuinely discriminating axis that separates ordered-domain clusters from IDR clusters, and it is the quantitative backing for the M1/M5 disorder and phase-separation narrative. The corpus ghost is what turns an uninterpretable violin into a comparison.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — per-cluster quantiles plus three corpus reference distributions.

units.name: pLDDT bimodality indicator (protein clusters)
units.what_it_shows: Whether a protein cluster is structurally coherent (one pLDDT mode) or mixes ordered and disordered instances.
units.encoding: A small annotation on the pLDDT violin: 'ordered' / 'disordered' / 'mixed', with the fraction of members above and below 0.7 printed.
units.data_source: motif_full_annotations.parquet plddt for protein rows only (254,466 non-null, 0 for UTR).
interactions: click 'mixed' -> splits the member table into the two populations
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A median alone hides bimodality, and a bimodal pLDDT cluster is a signal that the k-means bucket merged two structural contexts — directly relevant to whether the cluster's InterPro enrichment should be trusted for all its members.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — fraction above/below threshold plus a simple bimodality flag.

units.name: Region-conditional panel switch
units.what_it_shows: Not a chart but a layout rule with visual consequences: protein clusters get pLDDT, InterPro/MobiDB/ELM/IDPO/SignalP and no positional-RBP lane; UTR clusters get eCLIP/PAR-CLIP/iCLIP/miRNA and no pLDDT panel at all.
units.encoding: n/a — determines which units render.
units.data_source: Cluster prefix (prot_/utr3_/utr5_), verified perfectly consistent with the region column across all 889,215 rows (crosstab is exactly diagonal).
interactions: none
units.why_it_earns_its_place: One generic template would render an empty pLDDT panel on 600 pages and an empty InterPro panel on 600 pages. The prefix is a reliable switch, so there is no reason to pay that cost.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Cluster-versus-all-clusters context scatter
units.what_it_shows: This cluster's position in the whole 900-cluster space on two chosen axes, so its size, distinctiveness and annotation depth are read as relative rather than absolute.
units.encoding: Small scatter of all 900 clusters (x = n_instances, y = n_genes by default), points coloured by module with grey for the 387 unassigned, this cluster ringed and labelled. Axis pair switchable to (median pLDDT, median score), (coverage, n_partners), (n_sig_terms, n_genes).
units.data_source: Precomputed clusters.json rows built from groupby on motif_full_annotations.parquet plus partner counts from protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv and term counts from cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz.
interactions: switch axis pair
hover another point -> that cluster's card
click -> navigate there
brush -> 'compare these clusters'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The brief asks for 'this cluster vs all clusters' and 900 points is a trivial render. It is the only unit that answers 'is this cluster unusual?' — a question a reader has on every page and that no per-cluster statistic answers on its own. It doubles as the navigation surface between clusters.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — a single 900-row table (~200 KB) shipped once and reused on every cluster page.

units.name: Percentile rails on every headline statistic
units.what_it_shows: For each scalar on the page (size, coverage, median score, median pLDDT, partner count, term count), where it falls in the 900-cluster distribution.
units.encoding: A 60px hairline rail under each number with a marker at this cluster and faint ticks at p10/p50/p90.
units.data_source: Corpus quantiles computed once from clusters.json.
interactions: hover -> 'p73 of 900 clusters'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It converts every isolated number on the page into a calibrated one at near-zero cost, and it is the cheapest possible version of the 'vs all clusters' requirement — present on every stat rather than confined to one scatter.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — quantile arrays per statistic.

units.name: Partner cluster table with evidence-tier toggle
units.what_it_shows: The ranked cross-modal partner clusters — the literal answer to 'how does this motif interact with protein features' — under an explicit, reader-chosen evidence threshold.
units.encoding: Rows sorted by phylo_corrected_score, showing partner id, its auto-name, phylo_corrected_score, npmi_mip_APC, co_count, and the four gate values inline. Tier control is a radio with the resulting count printed in each label so the cost of relaxing is visible before clicking.
units.data_source: .../sequence_analysis_v4_0621/results/protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv (180,000 rows; cols protein, utr, co_count, n_indep_families, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF, npmi_raw, npmi_mip_APC, npmi_reweighted, npmi_family, perm_z_withinfamily, perm_p_withinfamily, passes_phylo_filter, phylo_corrected_score). MEASURED tiers: STRICT passes_phylo_filter 2,620 edges, 318/600 UTR clusters (median 5 partners, p90 23, max 39) and 201/300 protein (median 8, p90 35, max 62); RELAXED npmi_mip_APC>0.10 7,210 edges, 537/600 UTR (median 8, max 58) and 298/300 protein.
interactions: tier toggle
sort
expand a row for the partner's top features
click -> the pair page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is the half of R2 that no other unit can supply. The two tiers nest exactly (every passing pair has npmi_mip_APC >= 0.1001), so the toggle is a clean superset relation rather than two incompatible analyses.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — pre-filter to passes_phylo_filter OR npmi_mip_APC>0.1 (7,210 rows, ~0.74 MB) and index by both endpoints.

units.name: Four-gate bullet chart per partner
units.what_it_shows: Each of the four phylogenetic-independence conditions for one association, as a value against its threshold rather than a pass/fail boolean.
units.encoding: Four compact bullet bars: clade_concentration (< 0.35), n_indep_clades (>= 8), npmi_mip_APC (> 0.10), co_count (>= 10). Value marker, threshold tick, pass tint. frac_co_ZNF shown as a fifth read-only bar on a 0-0.5 scale.
units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv / results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv. MEASURED over the 2,620 passing edges: n_indep_clades min 8 / median 13 / max 23; clade_concentration mean 0.265, none above 0.50; frac_co_ZNF max 0.400 with only 11 edges above 0.30; n_indep_families median 38, max 143.
interactions: hover -> the condition stated verbatim from MODULES_REPORT.md and what it controls for
units.library: none (CSS bars — must render inside table cells)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: The brief asks specifically how to show that an association survived or failed the filter. A boolean hides that some passing edges clear every threshold comfortably while others scrape through at exactly 8 clades. Showing the margin is what makes the filter legible as evidence rather than as a rubber stamp.
units.precompute_needed: No — the columns are already in the edge table.

units.name: Gate-failure diagnostic for the empty partner state
units.what_it_shows: For a cluster with no partner passing the filter, WHICH specific condition its strongest candidate failed — not a generic 'no results'.
units.encoding: Card naming the best sub-threshold partner, with the same four bullet bars, the failing bars in vermillion, and a sentence: 'this cluster's strongest association fails on clade concentration (0.61, threshold <0.35) — the co-occurrence is concentrated in a single protein family'.
units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv, best row by npmi_mip_APC among the cluster's non-passing pairs. MEASURED across the 282 UTR clusters with no strict partner, the best sub-threshold pair fails on: clade_concentration>=0.35 in 270/282 (95.7%), n_indep_clades<8 in 155/282 (55.0%), npmi<=0.10 in 63/282 (22.3%), co_count<10 in 16/282 (5.7%). Gates failed simultaneously: 1 gate 93 clusters, 2 gates 160, 3 gates 25, 4 gates 4.
interactions: 'show all sub-threshold partners' -> greyed list
link to methods explaining clade concentration
units.why_it_earns_its_place: 282 of 600 UTR clusters and 99 of 300 protein clusters land on this state — it is the modal experience on the RNA side, not an edge case. And it can be made specific: because 95.7% fail on clade concentration, the honest message is almost always 'this association exists but is confined to one protein family', which is a scientific finding. No design proposed anything beyond a generic empty state.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — the best sub-threshold partner and its failing-gate vector per cluster, one row per cluster.

units.name: Sub-threshold (near-miss) partner list
units.what_it_shows: Partners that did not pass, ranked, with their failing gates marked — so the reader sees the actual evidence landscape rather than a curated subset.
units.encoding: Greyed table below the passing partners, each row tagged with which gates it failed; a persistent 'below threshold' label on the section.
units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv non-passing rows for this cluster. Note the corpus threshold counts: npmi_mip_APC>0.05 admits 21,873 edges and lights up all 600 UTR clusters with a median of 33 partners — which is why 0.05 must not be offered as a default tier.
interactions: expand/collapse
sort
filter to 'failed exactly one gate'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Hiding non-passing associations makes the filter look like a curation step rather than a measurement. Showing them greyed, with the reason, demonstrates the filter is doing work — which is the same argument the RAW_top30 verdict table makes globally, applied locally.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — cap at the top ~25 sub-threshold partners per cluster to bound the payload.

units.name: Partner protein-feature roll-up
units.what_it_shows: Across all of a UTR cluster's partners, which protein features recur — the one-glance answer to 'what kind of protein does this RNA motif travel with'.
units.encoding: Horizontal bars of InterPro/MobiDB terms, each weighted by how many partners carry it and annotated with the best fold, with the contributing partner ids on hover.
units.data_source: Join of the cluster's partner list to cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz rows where region=='protein' and the significance gate passes. MEASURED: 2,614 of 2,620 gated edges (99.8%) have a protein partner carrying at least one FDR<0.05 term, so this panel is substantive on essentially every UTR cluster that has any partner.
interactions: click a bar -> the partners contributing it
hover -> fold, k, n, FDR per contributing partner
units.why_it_earns_its_place: This is the strong direction of the data and the most direct rendering of the requirement's exact words. It contrasts sharply with the UTR side, where only 45.0% of gated edges have any RBP/miRNA term — so leading a UTR cluster page with its partners' protein features rather than its own RBP annotation follows the evidence.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — the roll-up per cluster, since it is a join across two large tables.

units.name: Partner ego graph
units.what_it_shows: This cluster's immediate neighbourhood in the 519-node association graph, giving spatial context before the reader opens the full network.
units.encoding: Small bipartite fan: focal node centred, partners arrayed on one side, edge width = phylo_corrected_score, node fill = module colour, shape = region.
units.data_source: results/phylo_corrected_candidates.csv filtered to rows touching this cluster; node positions from the build-time frozen layout; modules.json for colour.
interactions: click a partner node -> that cluster
'open in network' preserving focus
toggle to include sub-threshold partners as dashed stubs
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Partner counts are UI-friendly (median 5, max 62 protein-side), so an ego graph is legible where the full graph is not, and it gives the reader a spatial handle before committing to R3. It is also the natural place to show that a partner is cross-module.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — reuse the frozen network layout so the ego view and the full view agree.

units.name: Local raw-NPMI versus APC-corrected scatter
units.what_it_shows: What the average-product correction did to THIS cluster's partner ranking — which candidates were promoted and which were deflated.
units.encoding: Small scatter, x = npmi_raw, y = npmi_mip_APC, one point per candidate partner, passing pairs coloured, a y=x reference line; points far below the line are the promiscuity-deflated ones.
units.data_source: protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv npmi_raw and npmi_mip_APC for this cluster's 300 or 600 candidate partners. MEASURED: corpus-wide Spearman between the two is 0.981, and APC changes the #1 partner for 126 of 600 UTR clusters (21.0%). npmi_raw corpus range -0.739 to 0.901.
interactions: hover -> both values and the rank change
click -> the pair page
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It localises a global methods claim to the cluster in front of the reader. Priced honestly as 'nice' rather than 'must' precisely because I measured its effect: at Spearman 0.981 APC is a modest reranker, and the real work is done by the clade-concentration gate. Overselling this panel would misattribute the correction that matters.
units.precompute_needed: No — both columns are in the already-loaded edge slice.

units.name: Partner-count context chip
units.what_it_shows: How this cluster's number of surviving partners compares to other clusters of its region.
units.encoding: Chip reading '5 partners — p52 of 3'UTR clusters', with a mini distribution on hover.
units.data_source: Partner counts per cluster from protein_utr_FINAL_scores.csv at each tier. MEASURED strict-tier distributions: UTR median 5, p90 23, max 39; protein median 8, p90 35, max 62.
interactions: hover -> the region's partner-count histogram with this cluster marked
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Five partners means something different for a UTR cluster (median 5) than for a protein cluster (median 8), and readers cannot be expected to hold those baselines. One chip removes a systematic misreading.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — per-region partner-count quantiles.

units.name: Consensus-pair drill-down
units.what_it_shows: Which specific consensus strings on each side carry a cluster-level association — the finest-grained evidence available for a partner.
units.encoding: Expandable sub-table under a partner row: both consensus in mono, their coverages as bars, carriers, and the consensus-level co_count, npmi_mip_APC and n_indep_clades.
units.data_source: .../intermediate/consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz (49,547 rows x 22 cols: p_cid, u_cid, p_cluster, u_cluster, module, p_consensus, u_consensus, p_coverage, u_coverage, p_carriers, u_carriers, co_count, npmi_raw, npmi_mip_APC, n_indep_clades, clade_concentration, frac_co_ZNF, passes_phylo_filter, phylo_corrected_score, cl_npmi_mip_APC, cl_passes, cl_n_indep_clades). MEASURED: 1,430 of 2,620 gated edges (54.6%) have at least one consensus-pair row, but only 19 of 318 UTR clusters have NO consensus pair on ANY of their strict partners — so at the cluster level coverage is 94%.
interactions: expand a partner row
sort consensus pairs by npmi_mip_APC
click -> the carriers of that specific consensus pair
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the most scientifically informative drill-down in the whole portal, and my per-cluster measurement reframes it: the per-edge figure of 54.6% sounds like a coin flip, but from a cluster page the panel is populated 94% of the time. That difference is the argument for putting it here rather than only on a pair page.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — top 3 consensus pairs per (p_cluster, u_cluster), ~3,599 rows.

units.name: Consensus-pair fallback tiering
units.what_it_shows: Never an empty consensus panel: tier (a) the consensus PAIR where it exists; tier (b) each endpoint's own consensus list, labelled 'consensus per cluster'; tier (c) the most frequent literal member strings on each side.
units.encoding: The panel header names the tier in words rather than implying tier (a).
units.data_source: (a) consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz; (b) consensus_meta.csv (451 clusters); (c) motif_full_annotations.parquet motifs value_counts.
interactions: hover the tier label -> why this edge has no consensus pair (all 757 cross-module edges have none, by construction of the consensus association step)
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Zero cross-module edges have a consensus pair, and cross-module edges include the M1-M5 link the manuscript itself highlights. Showing an empty panel there would make the paper's own headline cross-module observation look unsupported.
units.precompute_needed: No — a selection rule over existing artifacts.

units.name: Shared-carrier gene list per partner
units.what_it_shows: The actual genes carrying both this cluster's motif and the partner's — the concrete handoff from R2 back to R1.
units.encoding: Expandable chip list with a count, each chip a gene symbol linking to that gene's transcript view at one of its instances.
units.data_source: .../intermediate/consensus_presence.npz — Pc bool (18,068 x 275), Uc bool (18,068 x 951), aligned arrays p_cid, u_cid, p_cluster, u_cluster, p_consensus, u_consensus, genes (RefSeq ids). A bitwise AND of one Pc column and one Uc column yields the list. Cluster-level co-carriers come directly from co_count in the edge table.
interactions: expand
click a gene -> its transcript view at that motif
download CSV
units.why_it_earns_its_place: co_count is an abstraction; the gene list is the evidence. It is also the only route by which a reader can check an association against their own knowledge, which is what an expert audience will actually do.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — precompute the AND for displayed edges at build time so no numpy runs per request.

units.name: Carrier resolution selector
units.what_it_shows: That 'genes carrying this motif' has three different answers depending on resolution — module, cluster, or consensus — with the active level always named.
units.encoding: Three-state segmented control with the count printed inside each option, plus a persistent caption naming the level that produced the number on screen.
units.data_source: Module level: .../03.interacting_modules/module_gene_members/module_gene_index.csv. Cluster level: motif_full_annotations.parquet gene_symbol per cluster. Consensus level: consensus_presence.npz. The same question returns roughly 1,562 / 175 / 51 genes for the prot_0040 x utr5_0004 case.
interactions: switch -> every gene count and list on the page updates and relabels
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the single most effective anti-misreading control available, because the three numbers differ by more than an order of magnitude and nothing in the underlying files signals which one a given panel used. Making resolution an explicit, visible choice prevents the most likely way a reader quotes a wrong number.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — carrier sets at all three levels for the displayed cluster and its partners.

units.name: Carrier tier badge (A / literal / fuzzy)
units.what_it_shows: In which of three senses a gene 'carries' the motif: tier A (the called instance is the literal motif at the called position), literal-only (the string occurs but was not called there), or fuzzy consensus carrier (PWM match above threshold).
units.encoding: Three-state chip on each carrier row with a legend and counts per tier.
units.data_source: Classification logic in .../motif_pair_network/m4_motif_examples/find_m4_examples.py, generalised across modules; per-instance data from motif_full_annotations.parquet, fuzzy carriers from consensus_presence.npz. The M4 audit found only 53 of 106 literal+carrier genes were tier A.
interactions: filter the carrier list by tier
hover -> the tier definition
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Without it, a reader clicks a carrier gene from R2 and lands on an R1 page with no visible highlight for the motif that put the gene on the list — a contradiction between two views of the same portal. The tier badge is what makes that expected instead of alarming.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — new computation generalising the M4 script across all six modules.

units.name: Cross-module partner flag
units.what_it_shows: Which of a cluster's partners sit in a different module.
units.encoding: A small module chip on each partner row; when the partner's module differs, the chip is outlined rather than filled and the row carries a 'cross-module' tag.
units.data_source: modules.json expanded to a cluster->module map, applied to both endpoints of each edge. 757 of 2,620 gated edges (28.9%) are cross-module; 3 have an endpoint in no module.
interactions: filter to cross-module partners only
click -> the meta-module view for that pair
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Nearly 29% of associations cross module boundaries, and the manuscript treats one such block as a finding. If the cluster page presents partners without module context, the reader cannot tell a within-programme association from a bridging one.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — module ids joined onto the edge table.

units.name: Enrichment dot plot
units.what_it_shows: The cluster's enriched annotation terms across all ten sources, ranked by effect size with significance encoded rather than filtered away.
units.encoding: Dot rows: y = term (display string), x = fold enrichment on a log axis, dot size = k, dot colour = source. Non-significant terms rendered hollow and greyed rather than omitted. A vertical rule at fold = 1.
units.data_source: .../intermediate/cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz — 260,572 rows x 18 cols covering ALL 900 clusters (cluster, region, source, term, k, n, K, N, fold, p, neg_log10_p, fdr_cluster, p_cmh, or_mh, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster, display, informative). MEASURED source rows: InterPro 143,254; eCLIP 38,097; PAR-CLIP 23,270; MobiDB 16,028; miR 15,798; iCLIP-P 12,679; iCLIP-C 9,519; IDPO 1,187; ELM 694; SignalP 46. fold on significant rows: median 21.5, p90 43.2, p99 100.2, max 387.6.
interactions: source filter chips with counts
significance gate selector
hover -> the contingency tooltip
click -> external deep link
units.library: d3-scale + custom SVG, or Plotly go.Scatter
units.why_it_earns_its_place: It is the 'annotations on the motif' half of the requirement, it covers all 900 clusters, and it is the only unit that shows effect size and significance simultaneously — which is what stops a reader from ranking terms by p-value alone.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — pre-slice per cluster after dedup, capped at ~20-40 rows. Terms per cluster after the triple gate and dedup: median 25, p90 91, max 148.

units.name: Significance gate selector (single versus triple FDR)
units.what_it_shows: Which FDR criterion is being applied, with the resulting term and cluster counts — because the authors' own script mandates a triple gate that is far stricter than fdr_cluster alone.
units.encoding: Segmented control: 'fdr_cluster < 0.05' / 'all three FDRs < 0.05 (as published)'. Each option prints how many terms survive for THIS cluster and how many clusters corpus-wide have any term at that gate.
units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz fdr_cluster, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster. MEASURED: fdr_cluster<0.05 gives 25,750 rows over 463 clusters (protein 297, utr3 123, utr5 43). The TRIPLE gate gives 14,525 rows over only 401 clusters (protein 297, utr3 73, utr5 31). The RNA side is where the difference lands: UTR clusters with any displayable term drop from 166 to 104 of 600.
interactions: switch gate -> the dot plot and table re-filter
hover -> what each FDR flavour corrects over
units.why_it_earns_its_place: MEASUREMENT NO DESIGN HAD: the gate that 10_cluster_term_enrichment.py mandates for display costs 62 clusters of coverage, almost all on the RNA side. Two designs specified the triple gate and two specified fdr_cluster alone, without either knowing the price. Making it an explicit control with the counts attached is the only honest resolution, and it tells the reader that 'no significant term' is a statement about a threshold, not about the cluster.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — carry all three FDR columns into the cluster shard so the toggle works client-side.

units.name: Enrichment table with full contingency
units.what_it_shows: The same terms as a sortable, exportable table with every statistic, so any claim on the page can be audited.
units.encoding: Columns: term, source, k/n, K/N, fold, or_mh, p, fdr_cluster, fdr_global, fdr_cmh_cluster, deep link. Significance shown as a pill using the active gate.
units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz, per-cluster slice. The universe is gene-level: N = 17,831 (protein) / 17,761 (utr3) / 17,045 (utr5).
interactions: sort any column
filter by source
CSV export
units.why_it_earns_its_place: A dot plot is a summary; an expert reader checking a specific claim needs the numbers. Export is what makes the portal citable rather than merely viewable.
units.precompute_needed: No beyond the per-cluster slice.

units.name: Contingency 2x2 mosaic tooltip
units.what_it_shows: The four counts behind an enrichment fold, so the effect size is auditable at a glance.
units.encoding: A 2x2 mosaic whose cell areas are proportional to k, n-k, K-k, N-n-K+k, with all four numbers printed and the universe named.
units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz columns k, n, K, N.
interactions: hover any enrichment row or dot
pin open with a click
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Fold enrichment ranges to 387x in this table, and a large fold on k=2 genes is a different claim from the same fold on k=68. The mosaic makes small-k terms visibly small, which no sorted column does.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Non-finite and zero-value guard
units.what_it_shows: Nothing directly — it is the rule that prevents the enrichment panels from silently breaking or lying.
units.encoding: or_mh values of infinity render as a capped marker with an explicit '>' glyph and the raw value in the tooltip, never as a point at the axis maximum. p == 0 rows use the precomputed neg_log10_p column and are annotated as 'below floating-point resolution' rather than plotted at infinity.
units.data_source: MEASURED IN cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz: or_mh contains 47,861 infinite values (18.4% of all rows) and ranges to 2.35e4 among finite ones; p == 0 in 11 rows, fdr_cluster == 0 in 11, fdr_global == 0 in 11, p_cmh == 0 in 55, fdr_cmh_cluster == 0 in 55; neg_log10_p is finite throughout with a maximum of 447.79 and 166 rows at exactly 0. fold is clean (no inf, no nan, min 0.00208, max 387.6).
interactions: hover a capped marker -> 'odds ratio is infinite (zero counts in one cell); fold enrichment is shown instead'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: No design mentioned this and every one of them proposes plotting or_mh or a -log10 axis. Nearly a fifth of the enrichment table would either crash a log scale or, worse, silently clamp to the axis maximum and appear as the strongest evidence on the page. This is the difference between a chart that is wrong and one that is right.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — sanitise at build time and store an explicit is_capped flag rather than relying on render-time coercion.

units.name: Display-string de-duplication rule
units.what_it_shows: Also invisible when correct: collapsing provenance-variant terms that render identically.
units.encoding: One row per distinct displayed term, with a small 'n sources' marker where variants were merged, expandable to the underlying term keys.
units.data_source: MEASURED: (cluster, display) is duplicated in 17,056 of 232,312 groups. De-duplicating on (cluster, source, display) leaves 3,865 collisions and ALL of them are MobiDB — e.g. prot_0000 shows 'binding mode context dependent (derived)' twice from derived-binding_mode_context_dependent-mobi and -priority, with identical k, n, fold and FDR. (cluster, source, term) is verified unique (max group size 1).
interactions: expand a merged row -> the contributing term keys
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Two designs specified dedup on (cluster, source, display) believing it sufficient. It is not — 3,865 groups survive, all MobiDB provenance suffixes, so prot_0072's top terms still repeat 'phase separation (curated)'. The correct rule is dedup on (cluster, source, display) keeping min fdr_cluster, which collapses these correctly because the variants carry identical statistics; the safe join key remains term.
units.precompute_needed: Yes — apply at build time, not in the UI.

units.name: Source filter chips with per-source counts
units.what_it_shows: Which annotation databases contributed terms to this cluster, and how many each contributed.
units.encoding: Toggle chips, one per source, coloured by layer (RNA #2E7D9A / protein #9C6B1E), each with a count; sources with zero rows for this cluster shown greyed rather than hidden.
units.data_source: cluster_term_enrichment.csv.gz source column per cluster; layer assignment from sequence_annotation/annotation_coverage_stats.json.
interactions: toggle a source -> filters dot plot and table
hover a greyed chip -> 'this database does not apply to 3'UTR motifs'
units.why_it_earns_its_place: Showing a greyed-out source is more informative than omitting it: it distinguishes 'tested and found nothing' from 'not applicable to this region', which is exactly the distinction the MobiDB region leak destroyed upstream.
units.precompute_needed: No.

units.name: Per-source coverage bar (denominator honesty)
units.what_it_shows: What fraction of this cluster's instances carry any annotation from each source, with the correct denominator — so a reader never reads MobiDB's 87.2% as applying to UTR motifs.

layout_options.pros: The identity rail answers "what IS this motif" permanently while the reader works through evidence, so the sequence object never scrolls out of view — which matters because the logo is the referent for everything in the tabs. Tabs keep four heavy panels off one page, so the initial payload and the visual load are both small. Region-conditional variation is easy: the rail swaps its positional histogram for a pLDDT distribution on protein clusters and nothing else moves. It matches the mental model of the data (a cluster is a sequence object that has associations) and it is the most conventional, so it needs the least explanation.
layout_options.cons: Tabs hide the partner panel behind a click, and the partner panel is the half of R2 most likely to be under-visited — a reader can leave believing the cluster has no evidence when its evidence is one tab away, which is exactly the failure mode for the 437 clusters with no significant term. Comparing annotations against partners requires switching tabs, so the roll-up of partner protein features cannot sit beside the cluster's own annotations. The 380px rail is expensive on a 1280px laptop, squeezing the dot plot into roughly 700px.
layout_options.best_for: The default, and the best fit for the RNA-biology wet-lab reader who arrives from R1 with one gene in mind, wants to know what the motif is, and will follow at most one link onward. Also the most forgiving layout for the coverage gaps, because the rail always has something to show even when every tab is thin.

layout_options.pros: The vertical order is an argument: direct measurement, then annotation, then statistical test, then association, then context — each step more inferential than the last, so a reader who stops early stops on the firmest ground and a reader who reaches the bottom has been walked through the epistemology without a methods detour. Nothing is hidden behind a tab, so the partner panel and the gate-failure diagnostic are always encountered. Numbered sections make deep links precise and reviewable. It degrades gracefully: a thin cluster simply produces a shorter ladder with explicit empty states, and the shape of the page itself communicates how much is known.
layout_options.cons: It is a long scroll — with 566 members, 40 enrichment rows and 14 relaxed partners this runs several screens, and nothing is side-by-side, so comparing the cluster's own annotation against its partners' features means scrolling between sections 2 and 4. The linear order imposes one reading, which frustrates a returning user who only ever wants section 4. The logo scrolls out of view by section 3, so later panels lose their referent unless a sticky mini-header carries it.
layout_options.best_for: The reviewer and the sceptical expert — the reader who wants to know what is measured versus inferred and will read top to bottom once. It is also the best layout for the manuscript-featured clusters like utr3_0215 and utr5_0096, where the honest story is precisely that sections 2 and 3 are weak and section 4 is where the evidence lives; the ladder makes that legible instead of looking like a broken page.

layout_options.name: C. Bilingual facing pages (this cluster | gate | partner side)
layout_options.pros: It renders the requirement's exact phrase — "how it interacts with protein features" — as a spatial relation, with the two modalities facing each other and the gate literally in the middle, so the filter reads as the thing standing between two claims rather than as metadata. Both sides use identical units on identical scales, which makes the protein/RNA asymmetry visible and honest: the reader sees at a glance that the UTR side has 7.4% RBP coverage and no significant term while the protein side has a 25.4x InterPro enrichment. The gate spine is the single best place for the four bullet charts because it is the only layout where they are the visual centre rather than a table column. It also makes the bilingual claim of the whole project immediately legible.
layout_options.cons: It is partner-centric: it shows one association at a time, so a cluster with 39 partners becomes a paging exercise and the ranked comparison across partners — which is what "partner-cluster ranking" asks for — is pushed to a strip at the bottom. It collapses badly for the 282 UTR and 99 protein clusters with no passing partner, where the entire right two-thirds of the page has nothing to show; those clusters need a different layout entirely. Three columns on a 1280px laptop leaves roughly 400px each, too narrow for a full enrichment dot plot or a 20-column table. It also privileges the association over the cluster's own identity, which is the wrong emphasis when the reader arrived from R1 asking about a motif.
layout_options.best_for: The mRNA-design engineer and the reader working the R3 network backwards — someone who already has a protein in mind and wants to know which UTR motifs travel with it, and who cares more about one association in depth than about the cluster in general. Best used as a drill-down mode reachable from layouts A or B rather than as the default entry point.

layout_options.name: D. Analyst dashboard (small-multiple grid, everything visible)
layout_options.pros: Everything is on one screen at once, so cross-panel reasoning is immediate — a reader can see that the logo is strong, the enrichment is empty, the RBP coverage is 7.4% and the partner evidence is real, all without a click, and form a judgement about the cluster in seconds. Uniform tile geometry means a power user learns one scan path and reuses it across hundreds of clusters, which is what makes browsing 900 clusters tractable. It is the best layout for spotting inconsistency (a confident logo next to an empty everything-else). Tiles collapse cleanly to an empty state without disturbing the grid.
layout_options.cons: It flattens the evidential hierarchy completely — a hollow non-significant dot plot occupies the same visual weight as a passing four-gate association, which is precisely the confusion the co-occurrence caveat exists to prevent, so it risks being the least honest layout despite showing the most. Every tile is too small for its detail: the enrichment dot plot cannot show more than a handful of terms, the partner table loses its gate bullets, and the member table is reduced to a strip. It demands prior fluency in every unit, so a first-time reader has no entry point and no reading order. On a 1280px laptop the tiles fall below roughly 300px wide and several become unreadable rather than merely compact.
layout_options.best_for: The first author and repeat power users doing comparative sweeps across many clusters, and the natural companion to a compare-two-clusters mode. It is a poor default and a poor landing page for anyone arriving from the manuscript, but an excellent optional density mode toggled from layout A.

layout_options.pros: It is the only layout that literally answers the requirement as written — "for a motif (instance or cluster)" — by starting from the instance and widening, so the reader never loses the thing they clicked and every cluster-level statistic arrives already framed as context for their motif. The percentile markers make the single most useful judgement immediate: is my motif typical of this cluster or an outlier? It creates genuine narrative continuity from R1, and the explicit zoom control teaches the instance/cluster/module hierarchy through use rather than through a methods page — which matters given that 5.91% of motif strings sit in more than one cluster. It also naturally answers "does my own gene carry the partner motif too?", which is the question that closes the loop back to R1.
layout_options.cons: It is wrong when reached from browse, search or the network, where there is no instance — roughly half the arrivals — so it needs a full fallback to another layout and the portal ends up maintaining two. Cluster-level detail is necessarily compressed to make room for the instance, so the enrichment panel, the member table and the full partner list all move behind links; a reader who wants the cluster rather than the motif has to click past the framing. The vertical zoom metaphor also competes with the page's own scroll, which can feel unstable.
layout_options.best_for: The wet-lab reader arriving from their own gene in R1 — by far the most common real entry into R2 — and the single best layout for making the instance/cluster/consensus resolution distinction stick. Strongest as a mode that layout A switches into when an instance id is present in the URL, rather than as the standalone design.

open_questions: BLOCKING, and it lands on an R2 page: the manuscript says 'MLXIPL ... contains the M2 utr3_0027 motifs', but modules.json assigns utr3_0027 to module 1 while the code that produced that figure (build_mlxipl_signatures.py, MLXIPL_M2_signatures.csv) uses utr3_0227, which is module 2. Whichever the portal uses, the cluster page for one of these two ids will contradict the paper. All file evidence points to a one-character typo. One email to the author; it should go before the cluster page is built.

Should the display significance gate be fdr_cluster<0.05 or the triple gate that 10_cluster_term_enrichment.py mandates? I measured the cost: the triple gate drops coverage from 463 to 401 clusters, and on the RNA side from 123 to 73 (utr3) and 43 to 31 (utr5) — so UTR clusters with any displayable term fall from 166 to 104 of 600. My recommendation is to default to the triple gate with the single-FDR view one click away and both counts printed, but this is the author's call because it changes what roughly 60 cluster pages say.

Should the STREME gap-fill be run before the cluster page is designed? It lifts logo coverage from 466 toward ~700 of 900 at a measured cost of about 2.4 CPU-hours (roughly 15 min at WORKERS=10), and the binary is present at /Users/wangyanz/software/meme/bin/streme. But newly generated PWMs will not match the matrices behind the published figures, so the page needs a provenance badge either way. Designing the layout against 466 and retrofitting 700 would be the wrong order.

Is the ZNF regex (^ZNF|^ZFP|^ZSCAN|^ZKSCAN) an acceptable proxy for the per-cluster artifact badge, or should it use the 36 protein classes from the aa 5-mer TF-IDF / truncated-SVD / Louvain procedure that the pipeline itself uses? The regex gives a defensible v1 (14 clusters above 40% ZNF, correctly flagging prot_0228 and utr5_0020 — both endpoints of the #1 raw-NPMI artifact pair), but it is not the same object as clade_concentration and should not be presented as if it were. Where are the 36 class assignments stored?

For the 437 clusters with no significant term, how prominent should nominal-p terms be? Showing them greyed is honest, but a reader who screenshots the panel loses the greying. Options: refuse to plot them at all and show only instance frequency; plot them with 'ns' printed inside each mark rather than only in the legend; or watermark the panel. I lean toward per-mark labelling, but it is a judgement about how the page will be misused.

Enrichment is gene-level against a universe of 17,831/17,761/17,045 genes, while everything else on the cluster page is instance-level. Should the page also compute an instance-level enrichment so the units match, accepting that the numbers will then differ from the published table, or stay gene-level and label the mismatch? Staying gene-level and labelling is safer; the risk is a reader comparing k=22 against the 566 instances shown two panels above.

No cross-reference exists anywhere in the trees to a known RBP motif database (CISBP-RNA, RBPmap, ATtRACT, Ray et al.), so the portal cannot answer the first question any RNA biologist will ask of UCUCC: is that actually the PTBP motif? TOMTOM ships with the same MEME install and could compare the 0.56 MB PWM bundle against a downloaded database. Is that in scope for v1, and if not, is the 'proposed in the manuscript, not measured here' badge sufficient?

The aligned-member strip, the per-instance PWM bits score and the carrier tier classification all require the same new computation: sliding each cluster's display PWM over its members and storing (raw_motif_index, offset, bits). Using the pipeline's own coverage() definition (COV_BITS=0.5, uniform background) would make the numbers match the published coverage figures. Is this build-time job approved? It is the single largest new computation in the R2 catalog and three units depend on it.

Should the partner table's default sort ever expose npmi_raw? I measured that APC changes the #1 partner for only 21.0% of UTR clusters and the corpus Spearman between raw and APC is 0.981 — so locally APC is a modest reranker and the clade-concentration gate does the real work. That argues the raw-vs-APC scatter is a 'nice' unit, not a headline, and that npmi_raw should stay unavailable as a sort key without a warning. Confirm the author agrees.

RBP names are unnormalised across the four CLIP columns (U2AF65/U2AF2, TDP43/TARDBP, UNR/CSDE1, IMP3/IGF2BP3, HNRNPH/HNRNPH1, plus opaque labels 'ACI' with 4,960 entries and 'SDOS'). Until a ~15-row alias map exists, every per-RBP count and every RBP facet on the cluster page is slightly wrong. Who signs off on the aliases?

Only 19 of 318 UTR clusters have no consensus pair on any strict partner, which is much better than the 54.6% per-edge figure suggests. Given that, is it worth re-running 17_consensus_association.py over the 757 cross-module pairs (which have none by construction)? For R2 specifically the answer looks like no; the need is on the R3 edge page.

Does a per-nucleotide NTScore aggregate over a cluster's instances exist or could it be built — a metaprofile of NTScore across all members aligned on the motif? The two HDF5 caches cover 5'UTR and 3'UTR at full resolution, so a cluster-level metaprofile is computable and would be a genuinely new visual for R2 (it would show whether a cluster sits on a score peak). No survey established whether the author wants this, and it does not exist for protein clusters, so it would be region-asymmetric.

Should protein clusters with very long members be handled specially? Protein motif_length reaches 535 aa while the median is 8, so a single 'motif' can be an entire domain and the word becomes misleading at that end. The length histogram surfaces it, but the logo, the aligned-member strip and the flanked-context strip all assume short spans.
